Control settings for zinbreg()

Source: R/control.R
zinbreg_control.Rd

Collects and checks the tolerances, iteration limits and other settings used by the EM algorithm in zinbreg(). Every argument is validated, and an invalid value stops with an error of class nbzinbreg_error_input that names the argument.

Usage

zinbreg_control(
  tol = 1e-08,
  maxit = 5000,
  trace = FALSE,
  start = NULL,
  hessian = c("analytic", "numeric"),
  hessian_check = FALSE,
  monotone_tol = 1e-08,
  grad_tol = 1e-08,
  zero_tol = 1e-10,
  zero_maxit = 50,
  nb_control = nbreg_control(tol = 1e-10)
)

Arguments

tol

Convergence tolerance for the EM algorithm. EM stops when the relative change in the observed-data log-likelihood, abs(new - old) / (abs(old) + 0.1), is below tol and the relative changes in the count coefficients, the zero coefficients and the change in log(theta) are below sqrt(tol), and the gradient check passes (see grad_tol). EM converges slowly when the zero part is poorly determined, so small changes between iterations do not by themselves show that the maximum has been reached; the gradient check does.

maxit

Maximum number of EM iterations. Reaching it gives a warning and converged = FALSE.

trace

Logical; if TRUE, print one line of progress per EM iteration.

start

Optional starting values: a list with exactly the elements count (the count coefficients), zero (the zero coefficients) and theta (a positive number). Their lengths are checked against the model in zinbreg(). By default the count part starts from a negative binomial fit and the zero part from a logistic fit of I(y == 0).

hessian

How the standard errors are computed: "analytic" (second derivatives worked out by hand, the default) or "numeric" (numerical differentiation of the log-likelihood with numDeriv::hessian()).

hessian_check

Logical; if TRUE, also compute the numeric Hessian and warn if it differs from the analytic one by more than a relative 1e-4.

monotone_tol

EM must never lower the log-likelihood, and each M-step must never lower its own part of the EM objective. A decrease is reported (with a warning of class nbzinbreg_warning_monotone) only if it is larger than monotone_tol * (abs(value) + 1), which allows for rounding error.

grad_tol

Threshold for the gradient check. The Newton decrement \(\delta = g^\top (-H)^{-1} g\) of the observed-data log-likelihood (with g its gradient and H its Hessian, both analytic) must be at most grad_tol: half of it approximates the log-likelihood that could still be gained, and every estimate is within \(\sqrt{\delta}\) standard errors of the maximum. EM keeps iterating while the check fails. The default 1e-8 means within 0.0001 standard errors.

zero_tol, zero_maxit

Tolerance and maximum number of rounds for the logistic IRLS M-step of the zero part. It stops when the relative change in its objective is below zero_tol and the relative change in the zero coefficients is below sqrt(zero_tol).

nb_control

Settings for the negative binomial M-step of the count part, from nbreg_control(). Its theta_min, theta_max and theta_warn also apply to the final estimate of theta.

Value

A list of class zinbreg_control holding the validated settings.

Provisional

tol, maxit and trace are part of the required interface. The other arguments are provisional and may change in later versions.

See also

zinbreg(), nbreg_control()
